residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must be an Australian citizen, domiciled in Australia, or ordinarily resident in Australia for at least 12 months immediately before the application (Family Law Act 1975 (Cth), s.39(3)).

waitingPeriod.description: No waiting period after filing. The 12-month separation period must be complete before the application is heard. Divorce Order takes effect 1 month and 1 day after it is made (Family Law Act 1975 (Cth), s.55).

noFault.name: Irretrievable Breakdown (12-Month Separation)
noFault.description: The marriage has broken down irretrievably, demonstrated by the parties having lived separately and apart for a continuous period of not less than 12 months.

basic.name: Application for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates divorce proceedings under the Family Law Act 1975 (Cth). Filed in the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia.

basic.name: Affidavit — Proof of Separation
basic.description: Supporting affidavit confirming the 12-month separation period

basic.name: Marriage Certificate
basic.description: Certified copy of the marriage certificate (or declaration if unavailable)

legalCitations.description: Federal statute — sole ground for divorce is irretrievable breakdown of marriage (s.48)
Procedural rules for family law proceedings
Federal legislation governing child support assessment and collection
Repealed presumption of equal shared parental responsibility (s.61DA); reformed parenting and property provisions (in force 6 May 2024)

filingFees.notes: Fee effective 1 July 2025. Reduced fee of AUD $375 available for parties experiencing financial hardship.

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Child support is assessed by Services Australia (Child Support) based on both parents' incomes, the cost of children, and the care percentage each parent provides.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: Spousal maintenance is discretionary. The court considers the applicant's ability to adequately support themselves and the respondent's ability to pay (s.75(2) factors).

effectiveDateRule: The Divorce Order takes effect 1 month and 1 day after the order is made (Family Law Act 1975 (Cth), s.55).
certificateNote: A sealed Divorce Order can be obtained from the court registry after the order takes effect.
